subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different kinds of hardware problems appear in these incidents?

judge.implied_focus: Characterization of hardware problems/failures in incidents (nature, scope, and remediation of hardware faults)

per_column.name: hardware_scope
per_column.rationale: Captures the breadth/locus of the hardware problem (single workstation vs. server infrastructure vs. site-wide), a key facet of distinguishing kinds of hardware issues.

per_column.name: intermittent_failure
per_column.rationale: Encodes failure mode (intermittent vs. persistent), a meaningful diagnostic dimension of hardware problem type.

per_column.name: requires_hardware_replacement
per_column.rationale: Captures severity/remediation of the hardware fault (replace vs. repair), a coherent facet tied to hardware problem nature.

judge.rationale: All three columns clearly centre on one inferable focus: the nature of hardware problems in incidents. They form a differentiated facet set spanning scope (where/how broad), failure mode (intermittent vs. steady), and remediation (replacement needed), which is a sound analytical structure rather than a single restatement or generic noise. The focus is actionable: an analyst can segment incidents by scope, isolate intermittent faults, and quantify replacement demand for capacity/asset planning. Minor deduction on structure because the set is somewhat thin and slightly remediation/scope-oriented rather than fully typifying problem CATEGORIES (e.g., disk/memory/network/power component type), which the query's 'different kinds' framing would benefit from; the large NULL rate in hardware_scope also weakens coverage.
